rationale: Jesus names the person and the event: "Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry? He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread" (12:3-4, BSB). 1 Samuel 21:1-6 is where that happens: "the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there but the Bread of the Presence" (21:6, BSB); in the BSB, "consecrated bread" occurs only in these two chapters, the Synoptic parallels and Hebrews 9:2. Graded explicit_reference rather than quotation because Jesus retells the episode without quoting its wording, and explicit because nothing is inferred to make the link, following conn-matt10-sodom-genesis19. Two checkable differences in the retelling: 1 Samuel 21 places the scene at Nob with "Ahimelech the priest" (21:1) and says the priest gave the bread to David, without narrating the companions eating; Matthew names no priest, while Mark 2:26 says "During the high priesthood of Abiathar," a difference from 1 Samuel 21 that commentators have explained in several ways. The rule that the bread belonged to the priests ("It belongs to Aaron and his sons," Leviticus 24:9, BSB) is what Matthew's "only for the priests" assumes; it is noted here, not authored as a separate row.
